lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Vermont businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Vermont is a rural state of small towns, independent businesses and well-known food and outdoor brands, and it bans roadside billboards, so being found online carries extra weight. We plan campaigns sized to a Vermont market and, where it fits, to the many customers who buy Vermont products from elsewhere.

sections.heading: Small towns, one small city and a lot of visitors
paragraphs: Burlington, on Lake Champlain, is the largest city, and with its neighbours in Chittenden County it forms the state's main population and employment centre. Montpelier is one of the smallest state capitals in the country. Rutland, Brattleboro, Bennington and St. Johnsbury are regional centres, and the remote northeast corner is known as the Northeast Kingdom. Along the Connecticut River, the Upper Valley around White River Junction shares its economy with towns on the New Hampshire side.

Then there are the resort towns. Stowe, Killington, Sugarbush, Stratton, Okemo, Mount Snow and Jay Peak bring skiers from Boston, New York and Montreal, many of whom own or rent second homes. Woodstock and Manchester draw visitors for inns and shopping. In these places the customer often lives somewhere else for most of the year.

sections.heading: The Vermont calendar: snow, mud, summer and foliage
paragraphs: Few states have such clearly marked seasons for trade. Ski season runs from early winter into spring. It is followed by mud season, when thawing roads and closed trails keep visitors away and many inns and restaurants take a break. Summer brings lake holidays, hiking, weddings and farmers' markets. Autumn foliage is short and intense, with inns booked far in advance. Late autumn, which locals call stick season, is quiet again before the snow.

A plan that spreads budget evenly across twelve months wastes it. The quiet stretches are the time to rebuild a website, shoot photographs and write content. The busy ones are for advertising and for keeping listings accurate.
bullets: Ad spend moved to the weeks when visitors plan each season.
Business profile hours updated for mud season and stick season closures.
Campaigns aimed at the metro areas your guests and second-home owners come from.
Seasonal landing pages for skiing, weddings, foliage and summer stays.

sections.heading: A Vermont name that sells beyond Vermont
paragraphs: The state produces more maple syrup than any other and is known for cheese, craft beer, cider, baking flour, ice cream and handmade goods. The word Vermont on a label means something to shoppers across the country, and many producers earn more from online orders and wholesale than from local trade. Gift-giving seasons, especially the end of the year, are their peak.
For these companies we work on online stores that are easy to buy from, product photography, search visibility for product terms, email and paid campaigns managed against margin and shipping costs.

sections.heading: Independent businesses and local trust
paragraphs: Vermonters tend to favour local, independent businesses, and communities are small enough that reputation travels fast. Marketing that sounds like a national chain works against you. Plain language, real photographs of your own people and premises, and honest reviews fit the market better. For trades and services, coverage areas matter, since a builder or heating firm may serve several valleys and should name the towns.

presence: TDM works with Vermont businesses remotely. We have no office in the state. Meetings are by video call, reports are shared online, and strategy, design, development and video are delivered by one team.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in Vermont?
faqs.a: No. We work with Vermont businesses remotely, through video calls and shared reports on an agreed schedule.

faqs.q: How should a Vermont inn or ski business market through the off-season?
faqs.a: Use mud season and late autumn for the work that takes time: site updates, new photographs, content and review replies. Reduce ad spend when visitors are not planning, then raise it ahead of ski season, summer and foliage. Keep your listed hours accurate if you close.

faqs.q: Can you help a Vermont food brand sell online nationally?
faqs.a: Yes. We build and improve online stores, shoot or direct product photography and run search and paid campaigns aimed at buyers across the country, with attention to margin and shipping.

faqs.q: How much does digital marketing cost for a Vermont small business?
faqs.a: It depends on scope: which channels, how much content and how wide an area you serve. We quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take for a Vermont business?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements, your current site and your competitors. We agree the timeline in the plan before work starts.
